title: Missing audit info penalties upheld
full_text:
The importance of correctly reporting audit information and auditor details has been emphasised by the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART), which has affirmed penalties against SMSF trustees for intentionally disregarding their compliance obligations.
The ART made the decision in the case of QQCS, CZMV, JRFK, PJXX and WHVG and Commissioner of Taxation [2026] ARTA 2159 in which the 2015 to 2018 annual returns for an SMSF named an auditor who never audited the fund, gave an audit completion date and recorded an unqualified opinion despite no audit having been carried out.
In the course of investigating the trustees’ action, the ATO was told by the auditor they did not audit the SMSF and the trustee who prepared the returns admitted they knew no audit reports existed, but returns were lodged to stop the fund being made non-complying.
The tax commissioner found that by declaring an audit was carried out by the named individual, the trustees had made a false or misleading statement and all trustees were held jointly and severally liable, including those who had left the administration of the fund to one person.
Consequently, the ATO imposed administrative penalties on the basis the fund had intentionally disregarded a taxation law.
As a result of these actions by the regulator and its rejection of objections raised by the trustees, who were all members of the same family, an appeal was made to the tribunal, which heard the case on 24 September before ART general member Joanne Dunne to decide whether the penalties were excessive and if they should be remitted.
In making a decision against the trustees, Dunne stated: “The applicants have not met their burden of proof to persuade the tribunal that the penalty for intentional disregard was excessive or inappropriately imposed.
“Intentional disregard requires dishonesty and actual knowledge that a false or misleading statement is being made. That can be inferred from the facts and circumstances.”
She also noted the trustee who prepared and filed the annual returns for 2015-2018 did not have any of the unqualified audit reports the return claimed had been received.
“[The trustee] signed the SMSF annual returns and declared (amongst other matters) the information in each return was true and correct. She knew it was not,” she said.
“She did this repeatedly, despite knowing that the details were false. She admits she did this to ensure that the fund was not found to be non-complying and to avoid the consequences of that.
“This demonstrates dishonesty and deliberation. The fund has flouted the requirements of the law.”
